login.setup_body: First-time setup: create the administrator account. You will use it to invite your team and manage settings.
login.login_body: Use your AgentGuard account to continue.
login.name: Your name
login.session_ended: Your session ended. Please sign in again.

run.title: Delete this run?
run.body: “{name}” and everything found in it will be removed.

agent.title: Delete the agent “{name}”?
agent.body: It is removed from AgentGuard together with its {n} runs. Your real agent is not touched and can connect again later.

agent_empty.title: Delete the agent “{name}”?
agent_empty.body: It has no runs. It is removed from the list.

scenario.title: Delete “{name}”?

rule.title: Delete the safety rule “{name}”?
rule.body: Agents will no longer be checked against it. Past decisions stay in the log.

user.title: Delete {name}?

key.title: Delete the key “{name}” for good?
key.body: It is already switched off. This removes it from the list.

demo.title: Remove all demo and sample data?

risk.intro: These runs look like they are heading for trouble. Start with the first one.
risk.empty_body: No run is above the warning level right now.
risk.summary_some: {pct} of the serious warnings so far turned out to be right.
risk.summary_none: Not enough warnings yet to say how reliable they are.
risk.rule_based: This is a transparent, rule-based score, not a trained model. Early numbers rest on few runs, so treat them with care.
risk.history_sub: Every warning, and whether it turned out to be right

trace.title: Investigation

shell.backend_down: Can’t reach the server. Check that it is running, then refresh this page.

Come back here to see how healthy your agents are.

bands.text: Many runs have problems. Start with the most serious ones below.

tile_waiting.label: Waiting for approval

overview.health_empty: Your agents haven’t been connected yet.
overview.activity_sub: The latest tasks your agents worked on

overview.next_sub: Based on what has been recorded so far

connect_first_agent.text: Connect your first agent so AgentGuard can start watching it.

send_first_task.text: Your agent is registered. Send its first task so AgentGuard can start checking it.

review_approvals.text: {n} action(s) are waiting for a person to decide.

create_safety_rule.text: No safety rules are switched on yet, so nothing is being blocked. Add a rule to protect sensitive actions.

run_reliability_test.text: Run your first reliability test to see how your agent performs.

all_good.text: Nothing needs your attention right now.

overview.fix_sub: The most serious problems, newest first
overview.more_note: Charts and extra numbers for people who want the detail.

connect.intro: Choose how you want to start. You do not need to write any code to try AgentGuard.

choices.title: Try it now
choices.body: Run a pretend agent right here and watch AgentGuard react. Nothing to install.

choices.title: Connect my own agent
choices.body: A guided path: get a key, download one small file, run it, and see your agent appear.

choices.title: Ask a developer
choices.body: Copy a ready-made message with everything a developer needs to connect a real agent.

connect.agent_hint: A short name, for example support-agent. It appears on every run and report.

try.title: Try a sample agent
try.intro: Pick a situation. AgentGuard will play it as if a real agent had just done it, and show what it noticed.
try.clean: AgentGuard checked the run and found nothing wrong, as it should.
try.note: Samples are simulated by AgentGuard and are clearly marked as samples. They are kept apart from your real activity and never change your numbers.
try.locked: Only members and admins can run samples.

steps.title: Name it
steps.body: Give your agent a short name.

steps.title: Get a key
steps.body: A key is like a password that lets your agent send its runs to AgentGuard. It cannot read your data.
steps.once: Copy this key now. It is shown only once.
steps.locked: Only admins can create keys. Ask an admin to create one for you, then paste it below.

steps.title: Download the file
steps.body: This small file already contains your agent’s name and key. It sends one sample run so you can check the connection.
steps.need_key: Create or paste a key first.

steps.title: Run it
steps.body: You only need Python on your computer, once.
steps.python_body: Go to python.org/downloads, download Python and open the installer. On the first screen, tick “Add python.exe to PATH”, then press Install.
steps.open_title: Step 2. Open a terminal where the file is
steps.open_windows: Windows: open the folder with the downloaded file, click the address bar at the top, type  powershell  and press Enter.
steps.open_mac: Mac: open Terminal, type  cd Downloads  and press Enter.
steps.expect: You should see “Done. AgentGuard received the sample run”. Then press the button below.
steps.next: I ran it. Check the connection.

trouble.a: Python is not installed or was installed without “Add to PATH”. Run the installer again and tick that box.
The AgentGuard server must be running and reachable from this computer. Ask whoever set it up.
The key is wrong or was revoked. Go back and create a new key.

steps.title: Check
steps.waiting: Waiting for the first run from “{name}”…
steps.waiting_hint: This page checks by itself every few seconds.
steps.ok: Connected. “{name}” has sent {n} run(s). (A test run does not count as real activity.)
steps.next_body: That file sent a sample. To connect your real agent, ask a developer: they can use the message from “Ask a developer”.
steps.dev: Get the message for a developer

dev.title: A message for your developer
dev.intro: Copy this and send it. It has everything needed to connect a real agent. The key is added if you created one.
dev.key_missing: (create a key first, or ask an admin)

activity.intro: What your agents have been doing, newest first.
activity.filter_empty: Nothing here matches this filter in the activity loaded so far. Load earlier activity to look further back.
activity.empty: No activity yet. Connect an agent and send its first task.
activity.end: That is all the recorded activity.

problems.test_title: Make a test from this problem
problems.test_intro: This saves a copy of the run as a test, so you can check that AgentGuard keeps catching it. All text is removed first; check what is kept below.
problems.test_catches: The test expects AgentGuard to catch:
problems.test_not_preserved: Cannot be tested from the copy (it depended on removed text): {list}
problems.test_none: Nothing in this run can be tested once its text is removed.
problems.test_confirm: I reviewed what the test keeps and removes
problems.test_saved: Saved. Find it under Test Library → Your own tests.
problems.intro: Everything AgentGuard found, most serious first. Each problem explains what happened and what to do about it.
problems.empty_none: No problems have been detected in the recorded executions.

empty_group.resolved: Nothing has been marked as resolved yet.

did.blocked: It stopped the action “{tool}” before it ran (rule: {rule}).
did.approval: It held the action “{tool}” until a person approved it (rule: {rule}).
did.recovery: It tried to recover the run automatically.
did.warned: It warned about “{tool}” but let it continue (rule: {rule}).
did.recorded: It recorded the problem. No safety rule was set to stop it.

problems.confirmed_hint: A rule checked this and it is a fact.
problems.possible_hint: A pattern that usually means trouble. It could not be proven.
problems.note_placeholder: For example: fixed the tool, added a safety rule

safety.none_registered: No agents are connected yet, so this rule will apply to every agent.
safety.scope_help: Choose which agents this rule protects.

agents.empty_title: Your agents haven’t been connected yet.
agents.empty_body: An agent appears here the first time it sends a run.
agents.sub: Click an agent to see its runs

connected.label: Connected
connected.hint: Sent a real run in the last {days} days.

quiet.label: Quiet
quiet.hint: Nothing received for {days} days or more.

test_only.label: Test run only
test_only.hint: Only the connection test has arrived. No real task yet.

waiting.label: Waiting for the first run
waiting.hint: Registered, but nothing has been received.

scenarios.title: Practice situations
scenarios.sub: Made-up agent runs we use to check that AgentGuard works
scenarios.intro: Each card is one pretend situation. Some contain a real problem AgentGuard should catch. Others are perfectly normal, and AgentGuard should not raise an alarm. We score it on both, so it catches problems without crying wolf.
scenarios.note: Click any card to see what happened, step by step. All of these are synthetic (made up for testing), not real customer data.
scenarios.search_placeholder: Type a word, e.g. refund or retry
scenarios.should_quiet: AgentGuard should stay quiet. No alarm expected.
scenarios.strip_caption: Each square is one step of the scripted run; red means a problem happened there and the ringed square is where it first becomes detectable.

drawer.find_nothing: Nothing. This run is fine, so AgentGuard should stay quiet. Raising an alarm here counts as a false alarm.
drawer.do: What AgentGuard should do about it
drawer.sim_note: only used when testing automatic recovery
drawer.hidden: The expected answer above is hidden from the detectors during a benchmark; it is only used to grade them.

add.help: Describe a scripted agent run and the answer you expect. The backend checks it before saving. The template below comes from the server.
add.ok: Added. It will be included in the next benchmark run.

admin.intro: The state of your workspace and who can do what.
admin.db_backup_note: A consistent copy of the database file, safe to take while AgentGuard is running. Keep it somewhere private: it contains your data.
admin.db_no_backup: Automatic backup is only available for SQLite. For PostgreSQL, use pg_dump (see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md).
admin.tidy_sub: Remove what you no longer need
admin.cleanup: Delete runs older than the keep-for setting
admin.roles_sub: Changing a role takes effect the next time the person loads a page

library.intro: Each test describes a situation an agent can get into and what AgentGuard should do about it. Run one to see how AgentGuard handles it.
library.search_placeholder: Type a word, e.g. refund, approval or retry
library.custom_sub: Tests your team added. They are kept separate from the built-in library.
library.synthetic_note: Built-in tests are scripted, synthetic situations. They show how AgentGuard reacts; they are not recordings of your real agents.

normal.label: Normal tasks
normal.sub: Everyday work that should go through without any warning.

incorrect.label: Incorrect information
incorrect.sub: The agent acts on, or reports, information that is wrong, missing or inconsistent.

repeated.label: Repeated actions
repeated.sub: The agent does the same thing again and again.

tools.label: Tool failures
tools.sub: The tools the agent relies on fail or do not respond.

safety.label: Safety and permissions
safety.sub: The agent does something it was not allowed to do, or breaks a rule.

privacy.label: Privacy protection
privacy.sub: Sensitive information is at risk of being exposed.

security.label: Security threats
security.sub: Someone tries to trick the agent into doing something harmful.

unexpected.label: Unexpected situations
unexpected.sub: Unusual or incomplete situations that are easy to mishandle.

prompt_injection_indicator.name: Resist instructions hidden in tool results
prompt_injection_indicator.summary: Text returned by a tool tries to give the agent new orders.
prompt_injection_indicator.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the hidden instruction before the agent acts on it.

sensitive_data_exposure.name: Protect sensitive information
sensitive_data_exposure.summary: Private details such as personal or account data appear where they should not.
sensitive_data_exposure.checks: Whether AgentGuard spots sensitive data before it is shared.

unauthorized_action.name: Require approval before important actions
unauthorized_action.summary: The agent performs a consequential action without a person's permission.
unauthorized_action.checks: Whether AgentGuard stops the action or asks a person first.

goal_constraint_violation.name: Respect limits and rules
goal_constraint_violation.summary: The agent goes beyond a limit it was given, such as an amount or a scope.
goal_constraint_violation.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the limit being broken.

workflow_invariant_violation.name: Follow the required order of steps
workflow_invariant_violation.summary: Steps that must happen in a fixed order happen out of order.
workflow_invariant_violation.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the broken order.

repeated_tool_calls.name: Prevent the same action being repeated
repeated_tool_calls.summary: The agent repeats the same action several times, for example the same refund.

infinite_loop.name: Stop endless loops
infinite_loop.summary: The agent keeps going round the same steps without finishing.
infinite_loop.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the loop and stops it.

repeated_failures.name: Stop retrying something that keeps failing
repeated_failures.summary: The agent keeps retrying an action that fails every time.
repeated_failures.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the retry loop.

invalid_tool_arguments.name: Catch actions built on incorrect information
invalid_tool_arguments.summary: The agent tries to perform an action using incorrect or incomplete details.
invalid_tool_arguments.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the incorrect details and proposes a fix.

contradictory_tool_results.name: Notice results that contradict each other
contradictory_tool_results.summary: Two results disagree, and the agent carries on as if they did not.

missing_required_evidence.name: Require verification before finishing
missing_required_evidence.summary: The agent tries to finish without checking the information it needed.
missing_required_evidence.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the missing check.

unsupported_success_claim.name: Catch claims of success that are not true
unsupported_success_claim.summary: The agent says the task succeeded although a step failed.
unsupported_success_claim.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the claim is not backed up.

tool_execution_failure.name: Handle a failing tool
tool_execution_failure.summary: A tool the agent relies on returns an error.
tool_execution_failure.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the failure and responds sensibly.

resource_exhaustion.name: Stop a task that uses too much
resource_exhaustion.summary: The agent uses more steps or time than the task should need.
resource_exhaustion.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the task running over its limit.

incomplete_execution.name: Notice a task that was left unfinished
incomplete_execution.summary: The agent stops part-way but behaves as if it were done.
incomplete_execution.checks: Whether AgentGuard notices the unfinished work.

normal.name: Everyday task done correctly
normal.summary: A normal task that goes through without problems.
normal.checks: Whether AgentGuard stays quiet when nothing is wrong.

unusual.name: Unusual but harmless task
unusual.summary: Something out of the ordinary that is actually fine.
unusual.checks: Whether AgentGuard avoids a false alarm.

expected.none: AgentGuard should let it through without a warning.
expected.escalate: AgentGuard should hand it to a person.
expected.request_evidence: AgentGuard should ask for more evidence before finishing.
expected.retry: AgentGuard should retry the action safely.
expected.correct_args: AgentGuard should fix the incorrect details.

technical.title: Technical details
technical.author_note: Description written by the test's author

run.intro: Choose what to test, check what will happen, then run it. Results appear on the Results tab.
run.step1_hint: Pick whole groups or individual tests. Leave everything unticked to run the whole library.
run.review_none: Nothing is selected, so the whole built-in library will run: {cases} situations.
run.safe_body: These tests replay scripted situations through AgentGuard's checks. They do not contact your agents, call your tools or change your data, so no real action can be taken.
run.synthetic_body: Results show how AgentGuard reacts to the scripted situations. They are kept apart from your real activity and do not prove how it performs on your agents.
run.no_permission: Members and admins can run tests.
run.timeout: The run is taking longer than expected. Check the Results tab in a moment.

results.intro: What happened in each test run. Every number below is counted from a recorded run.
results.none_title: No tests have been run yet. Run your first test to evaluate AgentGuard.
results.kind_note: Built from scripted situations. This is not real production activity.
results.headline: Is AgentGuard making agents safer?
results.headline_body: In {of} scripted situations, a safe outcome happened {without} times without AgentGuard and {with} times with it.
results.headline_not_enough: Not enough data yet. Run more tests to answer this.
results.caveat_title: Read this before trusting a high score
results.caveat: These scripted situations were used while AgentGuard’s checks were being built, so passing them shows the checks are consistent with their own examples. It does not show how they will perform on new situations from your real agents.
results.baseline_note: “Without AgentGuard” is worked out from the situations’ labels (any situation with a labelled problem counts as unsafe). It was not measured on a real agent.
results.exp_passed: AgentGuard found exactly the problems the situation contains: none missed, none extra.
results.exp_failed: AgentGuard missed a problem or raised a warning that was not needed.
results.exp_problems: Real problems in the situations that AgentGuard found.
results.exp_prevented: Situations with a problem that ended safely with AgentGuard but not without it.
results.exp_recoveries: Automatic recovery attempts that ended with the task safely back on track. Recovery is simulated in these tests.
results.exp_unnecessary: Warnings raised on situations that had no problem.
results.exp_delay: Average time AgentGuard added to checking each situation.
results.by_group_sub: How many situations in each group were handled correctly.
results.failed_none: Every situation in this run was handled correctly.
results.tech_intro: How often warnings were correct, how many real problems were found, and the other measurements behind the numbers above.
results.m_recall: How many actual problems were detected (recall)
results.m_f1: Balance between catching problems and avoiding wrong warnings (F1)
results.m_fpr: Warnings on situations with no problem (false-positive rate)
results.m_loc: Finding where the task went wrong (localization)

approval_card.what_the_agent_wants_to: What the agent wants to run
approval_card.note_required_to_reject_or: Note (required to reject or ask for changes)
approval_card.if_nobody_answers_it_is: — if nobody answers it is treated as rejected.
approval_card.only_members_and_admins_can: Only members and admins can decide.

flow.click_any_step_above_to: Click any step above to inspect its (redacted) inputs and outputs.

health_summary.share_of_runs_where_no: Share of runs where no rule found a problem
health_summary.a_run_is_flagged_when: A run is “flagged” when at least one detection rule fired.
health_summary.runs_whose_worst_finding_is: Runs whose worst finding is critical or high.

safety_rule_card.effects_line: In practice: stopped {blocked} · asked for approval {approval} · warned {warned}{watched}
safety_rule_card.effects_watched: · would have acted {n} times but was only watching

approvals.approved_the_agent_can_now: Approved. The agent can now run this action once.
approvals.actions_an_agent_is_not: Actions an agent is not allowed to take on its own. The agent waits here until you decide.
approvals.an_approval_lets_the_agent: An approval lets the agent run exactly this action, with exactly these inputs, once. It can never override a rule that says BLOCK. This page refreshes by itself.

history.actions_like_running_a_benchmark: Actions like running a benchmark or simulating a recovery will appear here.
history.one_point_per_completed_benchmark: One point per completed benchmark run
history.lines_going_up_are_good: Lines going up are good. If a line drops after you changed a setting, that change made AgentGuard worse at that job.

policies.name: Name
policies.would_trigger_of_tool_calls: {would_trigger} of {tool_calls_examined} recent tool calls would have been affected
policies.what_changed_kept_in_the: What changed? (kept in the version history)
policies.rolled_back_vv_is_now: Rolled back: v{v} is now the newest version.
policies.history_is_never_rewritten_a: History is never rewritten: a roll-back creates a new version, so you can always see what was in force when.
policies.stored_with_the_exact_inputs: Stored with the exact inputs each policy saw, so any decision can be reproduced
policies.rules_for_what_agents_may: Rules for what agents may do
policies.checked_before_every_tool_call: Checked before every tool call. Observe mode only records, warn mode only warns, enforce mode really stops the action.
policies.without_policies_agentguard_still_record: Without policies AgentGuard still records and detects problems, but nothing is ever blocked. Start from a template.

settings.connected_your_data_is_being: Connected — your data is being saved
settings.off_this_is_optional_every: Off. This is optional — every finding comes from rules and works without it.
settings.turned_off_anyone_who_can: Turned off — anyone who can reach this server has full access. Only use this on your own machine.
settings.software_agents_don_t_sign: Software agents don’t sign in: they use an API key, which can only send execution histories (see “Connect an agent”).
settings.applied_automatically_before_anything_is: Applied automatically before anything is stored
settings.largest_batch_of_events_accepted: Largest batch of events accepted in one request: {max_events_per_request}
settings.you_can_see_these_settings: You can see these settings, but only admins can change them. You are a
settings.delete_all_traces_older_than: Delete all runs older than {retention_days} days?
settings.set_a_number_of_days: Set a number of days first and save
settings.turn_off_a_rule_to: Turn off a rule to stop AgentGuard looking for that problem. Everything stored is re-checked when you save.
settings.turning_a_rule_off_also: Turning a rule off also means fewer real problems are caught in the Benchmark Lab, so you can see what you give up.
settings.rotated_name_the_old_key: Rotated “{name}”: the old key stopped working.
settings.a_key_lets_one_agent: A key lets one agent send its runs and ask for decisions. It cannot read anything. Keys are stored hashed and shown only once.
settings.ask_an_admin_to_create: Ask an admin to create or rotate keys.
settings.key_name_e_g_the: Key name (e.g. the agent it is for)
settings.your_new_key_copy_it: Your new key — copy it now, it won’t be shown again:
settings.name: Name
settings.issue_a_new_key_and: Issue a new key and stop the old one immediately
settings.everyone_who_can_sign_in: Everyone who can sign in to this AgentGuard
settings.there_must_always_be_at: There must always be at least one active admin; AgentGuard won’t let you remove the last one.
settings.share_the_password_with_them: Share the password with them securely; they can change it after signing in.
settings.password_changed_other_devices_were: Password changed. Other devices were signed out.
settings.changing_it_signs_you_out: Changing it signs you out everywhere else.
settings.there_are_no_passwords_to: There are no passwords to manage in local mode.
settings.pw_reset_done: Password reset; they were signed out.
settings.software_agents_don_t_sign@advanced: Software agents don’t sign in: they use an API key, which can only send traces (see “Connect an agent”).
settings.delete_all_traces_older_than@advanced: Delete all traces older than {retention_days} days?
settings.turning_a_rule_off_also@advanced: Turning a rule off also lowers recall in the Benchmark Lab, so you can see what you give up.
settings.provider_on: On, using {provider}. AgentGuard asks it only to explain problems it has already found; it never decides what is blocked.
settings.provider_off: Off. This is optional: every check works without it.
settings.provider_how: The provider is set by whoever runs the server, using these environment variables, so the key is never stored in the app or shown here: LLM_PROVIDER, LLM_API_KEY and LLM_MODEL. Restart the server after changing them.
settings.provider_sends: What is sent: the redacted steps of one run, only when someone asks for a diagnosis.
settings.retention_intro: Older runs are deleted to keep the database small. Set 0 to keep everything.

trace_detail.what_is_safe_to_do: What is safe to do next
trace_detail.agentguard_only_ever_previews_or: AgentGuard only ever previews or simulates here. It never executes a real tool.
trace_detail.try_it_in_a_simulated: Try it in a simulated environment
trace_detail.how_many_retries_will_still: How many retries will still fail first?
trace_detail.the_corrected_arguments_turn_out: The corrected arguments turn out to be valid
trace_detail.this_outcome_never_depends_on: This outcome never depends on the environment: a human decides.
trace_detail.members_and_admins_can_run: Members and admins can run simulations
trace_detail.viewers_can_read_the_plan: Viewers can read the plan but not run simulations.
trace_detail.a_language_model_reads_only: A language model reads only the relevant redacted events and offers a hypothesis. It is never treated as proof and never triggers actions.
trace_detail.ai_diagnosis_isn_t_configured: AI diagnosis isn’t configured, which is fine — every finding above comes from deterministic rules.
trace_detail.each_box_is_one_step: Each box is one step of the run, left to right. Red = error. Outlined = evidence for a finding. Click any step to inspect it.
trace_detail.not_determinable_from_the_recorded: — not determinable from the recorded evidence
trace_detail.earliest_step_at_which_a: earliest step at which a rule could prove it
trace_detail.no_failure_to_localize: No step to point to: nothing went wrong.
trace_detail.each_finding_comes_from_an: Each finding comes from an explicit rule, so it is a proven violation of that rule — not a guess.
trace_detail.no_rule_found_a_problem: ✅ No rule found a problem in this run.
trace_detail.each_check_happened_before_the: Each check happened BEFORE the tool was allowed to run
trace_detail.predicted_before_the_action_ran: Predicted before the action ran — separate from confirmed findings above

traces.no_traces_yet: No activity yet. Connect an agent and send its first task.
traces.send_traces_from_your_agent: Send runs from your agent with the SDK, or explore with synthetic demo data.
traces.no_issues_detected_this_run: No issues detected — this run looks healthy.
traces.each_little_square_under_a: Each little square under a run is one step, left to right. Red squares are steps where something went wrong.
traces.send_traces_from_your_agent@advanced: Send traces from your agent with the SDK, or explore with synthetic demo data.

roles.label: Viewer
roles.plain: Can look at everything but change nothing.

roles.label: Member
roles.plain: Can also decide approvals, run benchmarks and simulations, connect agents, load demo data and add scenarios.

roles.label: Admin
roles.plain: Can also edit safety rules, manage people, API keys and settings, and see the security history.
